target_customer: Women buying organic period products at retail
problem: Mainstream tampons and pads contain chemicals many buyers wanted to avoid, and period products are inaccessible to many women.
business_model: Consumer packaged goods with a one for one giving model

founders.name: Talia Frenkel
founders.background_notes: Photojournalist documenting humanitarian crises per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Contract manufactured consumer goods; difficulty was sourcing certified organic cotton and retail distribution.

defensibility.rationale: Product and mission model were copyable; brand and retail placement were the assets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: P&G bought L. in February 2019 to complement Always and Tampax.

market_need_then: Growing consumer demand for natural products and period equity; P&G cited the naturals segment as its reason to buy.

brand_strength.rationale: Mission driven one for one brand recognized by B Corp, Fast Company and Forbes per YC page, sold in major US retailers. Single letter name hard to search; origin not found.

outcome_analysis: L. combined an organic product, a one for one mission and a design led brand to win retail distribution in more than 5,000 US stores, which drew P&G to buy it in February 2019. The price is undisclosed; TechCrunch cited a person familiar putting it near $100M, which is unverified.
notes: Aggregators show only $120K (2015-08); not verified so no round recorded. Wikipedia says founded 2015 while a press source says 2011; founded_year follows the YC batch. Price roughly $100M from an unnamed person per TechCrunch, left out of exit amount. No competitor sources dated at the 2015 batch; LOLA (founded 2015, seed reported 2016-03) was left out because its source is dated after the batch.
